messages.content: Can we finish the Minneapolis airfare? I still have the hotel held May 19-21. Opening dinner is 6:30 Wednesday, and Friday breakouts may run to 1:00. Please compare the remaining nonstop round trips: fare, elapsed time, arrival buffer, Friday airport margin, and what time I get back to Chicago.

Here are the clean remaining choices, all nonstop ORD-MSP:

| Itinerary | Total | Wed timing/buffer | Fri return/margin | Back in Chicago | Trade-off |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| United | $293 | 1:05-2:38; hotel about 3:30, roughly 3 hrs before dinner | 4:35-6:07; leave downtown around 1:20 for 2+ hrs at MSP | 6:07 | Best timing, not cheapest |
| Delta | $249 | 1:35-3:08; hotel about 4:00 | 5:55-7:28; very safe margin | 7:28 | Saves $44, later Friday homecoming |
| American | $236 | 12:20-1:52; long Wed buffer | 6:45-8:18 | 8:18 | Cheapest, but drags out Friday |

I would skip the 3:20-ish return: it costs more than the cheaper options and is tight if breakouts really reach 1:00.
The 3:20 return is out, then. Is United worth the $44 over Delta?

For this agenda, yes. The United fare buys you an ORD arrival about 1 hour 20 minutes earlier while still leaving a reasonable MSP cushion after a 1:00 finish. Delta is fine if cost is the only factor, but United is the cleaner workday ending.
Any problem getting checked in before the 6:30 dinner if the outbound lands at 2:38?

No issue. Even with a normal deplaning delay, rideshare should put you downtown around 3:25-3:40. Light rail plus the walk is closer to 3:45-4:00. That still leaves time to check in and reset before dinner.
Okay, ticket the United pair. Standard economy is fine; aisle if you can.

Ticketed and saved to the Minneapolis file: United nonstop ORD-MSP Wednesday May 19, 1:05-2:38, and MSP-ORD Friday May 21, 4:35-6:07, total $293. Aisle seating requested/selected where available in standard economy. No rental car added. I also kept the note to leave downtown around 1:20 Friday unless the breakouts end earlier.

messages.content: Switching to a low-key personal trip now. Milwaukee June 25-27 with Daniel, train from Chicago after work Friday, museum exhibit Saturday afternoon, and brunch with my sister Sunday. Can you compare walkable hotels near the lakefront, Third Ward, or station and keep the total moderate?

Sure. One room with one bed? And for “moderate,” should I try to keep the two-night total under a particular number, or just avoid the pricier lakefront places unless they clearly solve the logistics?
One room, one bed. I’d like under $500 all in if possible, but show me if a better location is only a bit more. We’d rather not plan around a car.

I found four realistic fits, using refundable-looking public rates with taxes estimated:

| Hotel | Est. 2-night total | Walks | Breakfast / room basics | Dinner access | Cancellation | Best room to hold | Trade-off |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Homewood Suites Downtown / Third Ward | $454 | ~12 min from train, ~17 min to museum | Breakfast included; in-room coffee; full fridge/kitchenette | Public Market and Third Ward restaurants close | By Jun 23 | King studio, non-smoking | Best balance; not directly lakefront |
| Drury Plaza Downtown | $414 | ~14 min from train, ~18 min to museum | Breakfast included; coffee + mini-fridge | Downtown restaurants nearby; evening snacks if you arrive early enough | By Jun 24 | Deluxe king | Very practical, less neighborhood feel |
| SpringHill Suites Downtown | $376 | ~9 min from train, ~24 min to museum | Breakfast included; coffee + mini-fridge | Fine but fewer appealing late casual spots right outside | By Jun 24 | King suite | Cheapest; farthest from lake/Third Ward |
| Westin Milwaukee | $548 | ~20 min from train, ~5 min to museum | No breakfast; coffee/fridge listed or confirmable | Strong on-site/nearby dinner | By Jun 22 | Traditional king | Best museum location, but premium is real |

My pick is Homewood. It keeps you under $500, gives you easy Friday dinner choices, and avoids paying Westin money just to be closer to the museum.
For Friday night, we’d probably arrive around 8:45 if the train is on time. Which one is easiest for dinner without walking forever?

Homewood is strongest for that. You would be near Third Ward restaurants and the Public Market area, though some counter-service spots may be winding down. Drury is workable too, but it feels more like picking from downtown options within a 7-10 minute walk. Westin has the easiest on-site restaurant, but the room cost is much higher.
Does Homewood have an actual refrigerator, not just a tiny cube? And coffee in the room?

Yes. The king studio setup is a suite-style room with a kitchenette, so it should have a real refrigerator, not just a small cube, plus an in-room coffeemaker. I would still add a note on the hold to preserve the kitchenette room type.
How much more is Homewood than SpringHill once breakfast is considered?

About $78 more total, and SpringHill also includes breakfast, so the breakfast line does not erase the gap. The $78 is really buying the better Friday/Saturday neighborhood, easier dinner, and the more useful kitchenette/fridge setup.
That seems worth it. Please hold Homewood if it is refundable. One bed, quiet if available. Daniel does not need anything fancy.

Held: Homewood Suites Milwaukee Downtown, June 25-27, one non-smoking king studio suite, refundable, estimated total $454.20 with taxes. Added requests for a quiet room away from elevator/ice and noted likely Friday arrival after 8:30 p.m. Cancellation deadline saved as June 23 at 11:59 p.m. No train tickets or brunch plans changed yet.
